assumptions: Cases run against the live web through Codex web search; course pages change between runs, so assertions check structure, verdicts and exclusions rather than specific courses.
The timing window (120 to 21 days before the next start) and once-a-year offerings are assumptions kept as constants in SCORING.md.
Run success establishes artifact delivery. Ordinary cases also need a human check that each shortlisted quote appears in the linked document.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session with web search, at most 40 searches and 30 opened documents, 1800 seconds and one 200000-byte report. No managed-model routes or connected providers.
Cost grows with how many course documents are PDFs that must be read in full, and with how quickly the fit gate can stop a poor fit.
effects: Reads public web pages through web search.
No logins to course platforms, no email addresses guessed, no messages sent, nothing published.

cases.description: A field survey app. Courses in agricultural extension, public health and development economics collect household survey data; many use paper forms or a free competitor.

inputs.teaching_job: Design a questionnaire and collect household survey data on phones in the field, including where there is no signal.
inputs.alternatives: KoboToolbox, paper questionnaires typed into Excel afterwards
inputs.subjects: agricultural extension, public health, development economics

cases.description: A loyalty-stamp app for independent cafes. Courses do not have students run a cafe loyalty scheme, so the fit gate should stop early with no kit or notes.

inputs.teaching_job: Give coffee shop customers a digital stamp card and a free drink after ten visits.

cases.description: Same job as ordinary with a stated education offer and one region. The kit must use the stated offer and must not ask the founder to decide it.

inputs.teaching_job: Design a questionnaire and collect household survey data on phones in the field, including where there is no signal.
inputs.education_offer: Free accounts for up to 60 students per class for one semester; the instructor gets a workspace the same day.
